title: Enforce security-critical negative tests and coverage floors
goal: Define and enforce security-critical test obligations for authorization, tenant isolation and other trust boundaries, including stronger changed-code coverage floors where runtime code exists.
outputs: machine-readable runtime security ownership and negative-test policy
explicit not-applicable evidence before product runtime exists
fail-closed security-test audit for future product-runtime boundaries
invariants: security tooling cannot silently become a product runtime dependency
security controls fail closed when evidence is unavailable or ambiguous
heavy security checks are risk-adaptive rather than blindly repeated on every trivial change
security_properties: no production/customer data is sent to unreviewed external security tooling
security-critical changes cannot lower required gates or coverage floors
unknown tool or evidence identities are rejected
acceptance_tests: cmdr-dev validation-run succeeds for the selected plan
unit tests prove no-runtime state is not-applicable rather than passed
unit tests reject unregistered runtime boundaries
unit tests enforce active authorization and tenant gates when required
unit tests enforce 80/90 coverage floors and reject stale evidence
adaptive push and pull-request CI execute CHK-SECURITY-TESTS

performance_budget.rationale: security gates must preserve developer/agent throughput
metrics: fast source-level security gates remain PR-suitable
heavy dynamic security controls are scheduled only by explicit risk triggers

migration.rationale: engineering control-plane changes; no product persistent data

rollback.strategy: revert the security-engine lot while retaining the verified E3 adaptive/full-kernel fallback

required_checks: independent full-kernel fallback when CI/security control-plane changes require it
definition_of_ready: security scope is bounded and does not claim runtime product behavior
definition_of_done: security-critical scope has explicit ownership metadata
authorization and tenant-isolation negative-test obligations are machine-checkable
global coverage floor is at least 80 percent when measurable
new/changed security-critical code targets at least 90 percent coverage
absence of measurable runtime coverage before runtime exists is reported as not-applicable rather than falsely passed
